summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and recent right hip fracture repair was admitted from a rehab facility with fever, tachypnea, and respiratory distress. He was found to have healthcare-associated pneumonia with gram-negative bacteria, likely from his recent hospitalization. He required mechanical ventilation initially due to worsening secretions and hypoxia. Bronchoscopy with mini-BAL confirmed gram-negative rods, and he was treated with intravenous antibiotics, initially broad-spectrum and later narrowed to ceftazidime. His respiratory status improved over the course of the admission, allowing weaning from mechanical ventilation to trach mask support. He remained lethargic but arousable, with stable neurologic status and no seizures. He completed an 8-day course of antibiotics and was discharged to extended care with plans for ongoing tracheostomy care, physical therapy, and follow-up with multiple specialists, including for evaluation of mediastinal widening noted on imaging.
problems: Pneumonia due to other gram-negative bacteria
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Other dependence on machines, supplemental oxygen
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Aftercare for healing traumatic fracture of hip
